summary: Hisayoshi Miyamoto works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, and studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. He has held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (all attested 2026).

Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held academic positions at Koyasan University, where he served as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and later as a professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1992, he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Otani University, and was affiliated with Osaka University (attested 2016).

Hjalmar Frisk was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Gothenburg in 1918. He taught at Lund University (1937) and served at Gothenburg as PD (1927), acting professor (1931–1932), and professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics and Sanskrit (1938–1967).

Hla Pe was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon (~1933–1938), University College London (~1938–1939), and SOAS (~1940–1944). At SOAS, he taught Burmese language and culture from 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Washington by 1994, studying under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Hogen Bays works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada and served as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Hoin Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was a disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto (~1953–1986) and studied at Ryukoku University from approximately 1959 to 1963.
Hoju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University (~1999–2003) and KU Leuven (~2005–2007). He taught Kyokuga Saeki.
Hoju Shioda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. As attested in 2026, he held posts at Minobusan University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Hojun Nagasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1964–1967). He served at Otani University (~1970–1999, professor emeritus) and was president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies in 1998.
Hokai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and under Bunyiu Nanjio, later serving as a professor at Otani University (~1920–1947).
Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and held a post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holden Furber was a historian and Indologist who studied at Harvard and Oxford. He taught at Harvard (~1936–1940), the University of Texas at Austin (1940, 1945–1948), and was Professor of South Asia Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (1948–1973).

Holger Pedersen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald under scholars including Karl Verner, Vilhelm Thomsen, and Karl Brugmann. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen as PD, extraordinary professor, and professor from 1897.

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2000–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

Holmes Welch was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned his BA and MA at Harvard University (-1957). He later served as a Dozent at Harvard University (~1964–1974) and Yale University.

Hong Luo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, earning a PhD from Peking University in 2007. He worked at the China Tibetology Research Center (2007–2017), became professor at Sichuan University (2018), and is a research fellow at Hamburg (attested 2026).
Hongyue Guo is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007), studying under Stephen R. Bokenkamp and Xubang Qi.
